case_name: Wong v. AA Property Management Ltd.
text:
IN THE SUPREME COURT OF BRITISH COLUMBIA

Citation:

Wong v. AA Property Management Ltd.,

2013 BCSC 1551

Date: 20130827

Docket: S138380

Registry: New Westminster

Between:

Ed
Wong

Plaintiff

And

AA
Property Management Ltd.,

Aaron
Hung Kit Leung, Barbara Sau Chun To,

Eddie
Yeung Tak Chu, Winne Wong, Vasco Tin Yau Chu,

Jimmy
Zhi Min Chen, Christina Chui Yook Li,

Kam
Lun Ho, Ken Shao Tsung Chou and

The
Owners, Strata Plan LMS 2461

Defendants

Before: The Honourable Mr. Justice Jenkins

Reasons for Judgment

Counsel for Plaintiff:

In
Person

Counsel for Defendants:

M.
Libby

Place and Date of Hearing:

New
Westminster, B.C.

March
1, 2013

Place and Date of Judgment:

New
Westminster, B.C.

August
27, 2013

[
1
]

This is an application by the defendants under
Rule 9-5 to strike out several of the many claims made by Mr. Wong and that
those claims be dismissed on the basis that the allegations fail to disclose a
reasonable claim and that the claims are unnecessary and vexatious.

[
2
]

I have determined that the defendants are entitled
to the relief sought in the notice of application with a few exceptions. I will
briefly review the pleadings but for the purpose of brevity alone, will
necessarily group several of the claims under one heading where there are
common issues but first I will set out a brief factual background.

I.

Background

[
3
]

Mr. Wong is a co-owner of unit 807 in a
residential strata project located on Cooney Road in Richmond, B.C. The strata
corporation for this project is the defendant, The Owners, Strata Plan LMS 2461
(“the Strata”).

[
4
]

Mr. Wong’s claims are allegations that the
defendants have acted improperly in the management of Strata’s affairs.

[
5
]

The defendant AA Property Management Ltd. (the
“Property Manager”) was retained by the Strata in September of 2008 as property
manager and strata agent. The individual defendants are either representatives
of the Property Manager or are current or past members of the Strata Council.

[
6
]

On May 25, 2012 the Strata held its annual
general meeting (the “2012 AGM”) during which a new Strata Council was elected
by the owners and the owners approved a new operating budget for 2012-2013.

[
7
]

The Owners, Strata Plan LMS 2461 did not
authorize or approve of the prosecution of this action.

[
8
]

In addition to action No. 138380 Mr. Wong has
commenced a second action, No. 145263, against all of the same defendants as in
this action, with the exception of The Owners, Strata Plan LMS 2461. A notice
of application has also been issued to in action No. 145263 to dismiss all of
the claims in that action as well and my reasons regarding the application in
that action will also be delivered in these reasons.

[
9
]

Many of Mr. Wong’s claims can be categorized and
will be dealt with in these reasons in groups. For example, many of the claims
cannot be advanced by an individual owner but can be advanced only by the
Strata. These reasons will necessarily deal with the various categories which
are set out below.

II.

Overview of the Rules and Law Relating to an
Application to Strike

[
10
]

The applicable Rule is 9-5(1) which states:

At any stage of a proceeding, the court may
order to be struck out or amended the whole or any part of a pleading, petition
or other document on the ground that

a)         it
discloses no reasonable claim or defence, as the case may be,

b)         it is
unnecessary, scandalous, frivolous or vexatious,

c)         it
may prejudice, embarrass or delay the fair trial or hearing of the proceeding,
or

d)         it is
otherwise an abuse of the process of the court,

and the court may pronounce judgment or
order the proceeding to be stayed or dismissed and may order the costs of the
application to be paid as special costs.

[
11
]

By virtue of the opening words of Rule 9-5(1),
an application to dismiss may be brought “at any stage of a proceeding” which
means at any time up to up to and including a trial and a formal order has been
entered following the trial. (
R&J Siever Holdings v. Sunridge
2007
BCSC 632
)

[
12
]

In
Odhavji Estate v. Woodhouse
, [2003] 3
S.C.R. 263,
2003 SCC 69
, the Supreme Court of Canada, after referring to the
decision of Wilson J. in
Hunt v. Carey Canada Inc.,
1990 CanLII 90 (SCC)
,
[1990] 2 S.C.R. 959

stated:

The test is a stringent one. The facts are
to be taken as pleaded. When so taken, the question that must then be
determined is whether it is “plain and obvious” that the action must fail. It
is only if the statement of claim is certain to fail because it contains a
“radical defect” that the plaintiff should be driven from the judgment . .. .

[
13
]

Under Rule 9-5(1)(b), a pleading can be struck
or dismissed if it does not go to establishing the plaintiff’s cause of action
or does not advance a claim known in law.(
Citizens for Foreign Aid Reform
Inc. v. Canadian Jewish Congress
1999 CanLii 5860
) .

[
14
]

Finally, in the very recent decision of
British
Columbia (Director of Civil Forfeiture) v. Flynn,
2013 BCCA 91
referred to
the judgment of McLachlin J. (as she then was) in
Victoria Grey Metro Trust
Co. v. Fort Gary Trust Co.
(1982),
1982 CanLII 227 (BC SC)
, 30 B.C.L.R. (2d) 45 at 47 (S.C.):

[I]t may be noted that it is only in the
clearest cases that a pleading will be struck out as disclosing no reasonable
claim;
where there is doubt on either the facts or the law,
the matter
should be allowed to proceed for determination at trial:
Minees v. Minnes
(1962),
39 W.W.R.112,
1962 CanLII 350 (BC CA)
, 34 D.L.R. (2d) 497 (B.C.C.A.);
B.C. Power Corp. v. A.G.B.C.
(1962),

1962 CanLII 672 (BC CA)
, 38 W.W.R. 577, 34 D.L.R. (2d) at 211 (B.C.C.A.). If there is any doubt it
should be resolved in favour of permitting the pleadings to stand:
Winfield
v. Interior Engr. Services Ltd.
(1969,
1969 CanLII 706 (BC SC)
, 68 W.W.R. 383, 4 D.L.R. (3d) 533
(B.C.S.C.).

[
15
]

Before proceeding with a discussion of the many
claims advanced by the plaintiff, there is one preliminary response the
plaintiff has raised which is a submission that since the defendants have filed
a response to civil claim, they are now precluded from bringing this
application to strike out the many claims.

[
16
]

I do not agree with the plaintiff’s position on
this issue. Rule 9 - 5 (1) specifically states that an application to dismiss
may be brought. “At any stage of a proceeding . . . . “ which I understand can
be at any time until judgment is entered. I am referred to the decision of
Madam Justice Fenlon in
Hundal v. Border Carrier Ltd.
2011 BCSC 1703
in
which the learned Justice granted an order under Rule 9 - 5 (1) on the first
day of trial and the lack of any authority in our Rules or decisions of our
courts prohibiting an application under Rule 9 - 5 (1) upon the filing of a
response to civil claim.

[
17
]

The notice of civil claim in this proceeding is
48 pages long and in that document the plaintiff seeks damages which have been
summarized by counsel for the defendants as follows:

(a)        claims pertaining to smoking and
ash bins;

(b)        claims pertaining to the
alteration and repair of common property;

(c)        claims pertaining to surveillance
cameras;

(d)        claims
relating to alleged refusal to give the plaintiff access to Strata records;

(e)        claims
relating to reimbursement and other payments made from Strata funds to the
property manager and/or Strata Council members;

(f)        claims
relating to parking rules;

(g)        claims
relating to denial of hearing at Strata Council meetings;

(h)        claims
relating to defamation;

(i)         claims
relating to access to the Strata’s office and assault;

(j)         claims
pertaining to voting at a May 27, 2011 Annual General Meeting;

(k)        claims
relating to conduct by Strata Council members after a May 27, 2011 Annual
General Meeting; and

(l)         claims
relating to an August 24, 2011 Strata Council meeting.

III.

Powers to Sue under the Strata Property Act

[
18
]

Firstly, as was stated by Madam Justice Sinclair
Prowse in
Extra Gift Exchange Inc., et al v. Ernest & Twins Ventrues
(PP) Ltd., et al

2007 BCSC 426
,

[50]      As far as the legal principles
governing standing are concerned, as is set out in
The Conduct of Civil
Litigation in British Columbia
(Peter Fraser & John Horn, vol. 1
(Vancouver:Buttersworths, 1978) at 105], a potential litigant must have the
legal capacity to sue or be sued and must be a necessary or proper party to the
proceeding.

[51]      As  review of Thomas Cromwell’s
Locus
Standi: A Commentary on the Law of Standing in Canada
(Toronto: Carswell,
1986) discloses, to be a necessary or proper party requires that the potential
litigant fall within the category of person or entity legally entitled to the
relief sought - that is, he/she/it may only pursue claims in which he/she/it
has a legally recognized interest in the claims made.

[72]      In any event, the plaintiffs do not
have standing to bring these claims on behalf of the strata corporation. As the
plaintiffs do not have standing to bring them, it is plain and obvious that
they will fail. Consequently, these claims are not only struck, they are also
dismissed.

[
19
]

In order to determine if the plaintiff in this
case does have standing or the capacity to sue we must look at the applicable
legislation and in this case it is necessary to review the applicable portions
of the
Strata Property Act
[SBC 1998] c. 43 (“the Act”).

[
20
]

The following sections of the
Act
are relevant
to this proceeding and notice of application save for claims by an owner to
seek relief against council members in “conflict of interest” situations;

2 (1) From the time the strata plan is
deposited in a land title office,

(a) a strata
corporation is established, and

(b) the owners of the strata lots in the
strata plan are members of the strata corporation under the name “The Owners,
Strata Plan [registration number of the strata plan]

[
21
]

Therefore, a strata corporation is created and
is a separate legal entity. Each individual owner of a strata lot is a member
of the strata corporation established on the filing of the Strata Plan which in
this case is Strata Plan LMS 2461.

3          Except
as otherwise provided in this
Act
, the strata corporation is responsible for
managing and maintaining the common property and common assets of the strata
corporation for the benefit of the owners.

[
22
]

Section 3 states that it is the strata
corporation, not individual owners, that is responsible for the management and
maintenance of the common property and common assets of the strata corporation.
“Common property” is defined in section 1 and generally is “any part of the
land and buildings shown on a strata plan that is not part of a strata lot”,
ie. strata lots owned by the individual owners. “Common asset” is also defined
in section 1 and generally includes personal property held by a strata
corporation and land of a strata corporation not shown on the strata plan.

[
23
]

Section 4 provides for how the strata
corporation is to carry out its powers and duties as follows:

4          The
powers and duties of the strata corporation must be exercised and performed by
a council, unless this
Act
, the regulations or the bylaws provide otherwise.

[
24
]

Part 4 of the
Act
, which includes
sections 25

through 34.1 inclusive, provide for governance of the strata corporation
through the council elected by the individual owners of strata lots contained
in the Strata Plan.

[
25
]

Consistent with the responsibilities of the
strata plan to manage and maintain the common property and common assets of the
strata corporation,
section 171
of the
Act
allows the strata corporation the
statutory right to commence an action as representative of all owners about
matters affecting the strata corporation. Specifically, section 171 (1)
provides:

171 (1) The strata corporation may sue as
representative of all owners, except any who are being sued, about any matter affecting
the strata corporation, including any of the following matters:

(a) the
interpretation or application of this
Act
, the regulations, the bylaws or the
rules;

(b) the common
property or common assets;

(c) the use or
enjoyment of a strata lot;

(d) money owing, including money owing as a
fine, under this
Act
, the bylaws or rules.

[
26
]

Before suing for the matters listed in section
171 (1), a strata corporation must obtain a resolution authorized by a ¾ vote
of the owners at an annual or special general meeting of the owners.

171 (2) Before
the strata corporation sues under this section, the suit must be authorized by
a resolution passed by a ¾ vote at an annual or special general meeting.

[
27
]

The ability of an owner to sue a strata
corporation is described in
sections 163
-
165
of the
Act
:

163 (1) The strata
corporation may be sued as representative of the owners with respect to any
matter relating to the common property, common assets, bylaws or rules, or
involving an act or omission of the strata corporation.

(2) An owner may sue the strata corporation.

164 (1) On
application of an owner or tenant, the Supreme Court may make any interim or
final order it considers necessary to prevent or remedy a significantly unfair

(a) action or
threatened action by, or decision of, the strata corporation, including the
council, in relation to the owner or tenant, or

(b) exercise of
voting rights by a person who holds 50% or more of the votes, including
proxies, at an annual or special general meeting.

(2) For the purposes of subsection (1), the
court may

(a) direct or
prohibit an act of the strata corporation, the council, or the person who holds
50% or more of the votes,

(b) vary a
transaction or resolution, and

(c) regulate the
conduct of the strata corporation's future affairs.

165 On application
of an owner, tenant, mortgagee of a strata lot or interested person, the
Supreme Court may do one or more of the following:

(a) order the
strata corporation to perform a duty it is required to perform under this
Act
,
the bylaws or the rules;

(b) order the
strata corporation to stop contravening this
Act
, the regulations, the bylaws
or the rules;

(c) make any other orders it considers
necessary to give effect to an order under paragraph (a) or (b).

[
28
]

In the case of
Ang v. Spectra Management
Services et al
2002 BCSC 1544
, Mr. Justice Lowry (as he then was)
interpreted the scope of section 164 (1) and stated as follows at para. 21.:

In my view, s.
164 (1) does no more than authorize proceedings by an owner to redress the
actions of a strata corporation that are significantly unfair to that owner. As
Sunbelt suggests, it is not unlike statutory oppression remedies that are
available to the shareholders or members of a company.

[
29
]

Based upon the finding in
Ang
, in order
for this action to be commenced and maintained by Mr. Wong against the strata
corporation, Mr. Wong would have to prove that some action or actions of the
strata corporation are “significantly unfair” to Mr. Wong in particular as
opposed to other owners of strata lots.

[
30
]

Sections 32 and 33 permit individual owners to
seek relief from council members of the strata corporation, as opposed to
seeking relief against the strata corporation, in what are considered to be
“conflict of interest” situations. Those sections are as follows:

32 A council member
who has a direct or indirect interest in

(a) a contract or
transaction with the strata corporation, or

(b) a matter that
is or is to be the subject of consideration by the council, if that interest
could result in the creation of a duty or interest that materially conflicts
with that council member's duty or interest as a council member,

must

(c) disclose fully
and promptly to the council the nature and extent of the interest,

(d) abstain from
voting on the contract, transaction or matter, and

(e) leave the
council meeting

(i) while the
contract, transaction or matter is discussed, unless asked by council to be
present to provide information, and

(ii) while the
council votes on the contract, transaction or matter.

33 (1) If a council
member who has an interest in a contract or transaction fails to comply with
section 32, the strata corporation or an owner may apply for an order under
subsection (3) of this section to a court having jurisdiction unless, after
full disclosure of the nature and extent of the council member's interest in
the contract or transaction, the contract or transaction is ratified by a resolution
passed by a 3/4 vote at an annual or special general meeting.

(2) For the purposes of the 3/4 vote
referred to in subsection (1), a person who has an interest in the contract or
transaction is not an eligible voter.

(3) If, on application under subsection (1),
the court finds that the contract or transaction was unreasonable or unfair to
the strata corporation at the time it was entered into, the court may do one or
more of the following:

(a) set aside the
contract or transaction if no significant injustice will be caused to third
parties;

(b) if the council
member has not acted honestly and in good faith, require the council member to
compensate the strata corporation or any other person for a loss arising from
the contract or transaction, or from the setting aside of the contract or
transaction;

(c) require the council member to pay to
the strata corporation any profit the council member makes as a consequence of
the contract or transaction.

[
31
]

The defendants, Eddie Yeung Tak Chu, Winnie
Wong, Vasco Tin Yau Chu, Jimmy Zhi Min Chen, Christina Chui Yook Li, Kam Lun Ho
and Ken Shao Tsung Chou are all either former or current members of the strata
council which I will refer to collectively as the “Council Members.”

[
32
]

Sections 32 and 33 were considered by the Court
of Appeal in the case of
Dockside Brewing Co. Ltd. v. Strata Plan LMS 3837,
2007
BCCA 183
. Writing for the majority in that case, Madam Justice Levine stated:

[59]      Section
33 provides remedies for breaches of ss. 31 and 32. A strata corporation or an
owner may apply for an order under s. 33 (3) “if a council member who has an
interest in a contract or transaction fails to comply with section 32 . . . “.
Under s. 33 (3), the court may make an order, if it “finds that the contract or
transaction was unreasonable or unfair to the strata corporation at the time it
was entered into . . . . “  Under s. 33 (3) “if the council member has not
acted honestly and in good faith, [the court may] require the council member to
compensate the strata corporation or any other person for a loss arising from
the contract or transaction . . . “

[
33
]

The Court of Appeal did not provide for any
additional rights upon owners to commence and maintain an action in this court
against current or former council members other than set out in the above
paragraph.

[
34
]

Next, there is a limited exception to the
limitation to the ability of only a strata corporation being able to sue in
respect of common property.
Section 171
, which is reproduced above, permits
suits regarding common property to be brought by a strata corporation as the
representative of all of the owners regarding the common property, ie. such
actions would require a ¾ majority of the owners to authorize the action. That
limited exception is set out in the Court of Appeal decision in
Hamilton v.
Ball

2006 BCCA 243
which held that an owner may sue a third party for
injury to the plaintiff proportionate share of common property.

[
35
]

To summarize the standing or capacity of an
individual owner to sue the strata corporation of which that owner is a member
is limited by the
Act
to two possibilities. Firstly an owner may sue the strata
corporation under
section 164
of the Act in cases where the actions of the
strata corporation have been “significantly unfair” to the plaintiff as opposed
to other owners 171. Secondly, there is a limited exception to the traditional
rule that only a strata corporation may sue regarding matters affecting the
strata corporation and that exception, following the decision in
Hamilton v.
Ball
, is to allow an owner to sue for only their proportionate share of
common property where a third party causes injury to that property.

[
36
]

Finally in summation, an owner can sue a council
member only in instances where the council member is in breach of the “conflict
of interest” sections of
section 32
of the
Act
.

[
37
]

It is with these limitations in mind that I will
review the various claims of the plaintiff to determine the claims are to be
struck and dismissed, whether the claims require an amendment to give rise to a
claim or whether the claims may proceed as currently pleaded.

IV.

CLAIMS IN ACTION NO. 138380

A.

Installation of Smoking and Ash Bins

[
38
]

In 2009 the council approved the installation of
wall mounted ash bins which were subsequently determined to be unnecessary.
Details of these claims are set out in paras. 37-43 of the notice of civil claim.
If there was any loss in this respect, the loss was that of the strata
corporation only and was not a loss peculiar to the plaintiff. The relief
sought is set out in paragraphs 1-2 of the Relief Sought section of the notice
of civil claim. The claims include an allegation that the Property Manager and
its employees acted contrary to the interests of the strata. Only the strata
corporation could advance such a claim against the Property Manager and its
employees as it is the strata corporation that has or had a contract with the
Property Manager. As well, the claims in this respect against the Council
Members are not within the provisions of
sections 32
and 33 and therefore
disclose no cause of action. Accordingly, claims 1 and 2 of the Claims Sought
are struck and dismissed.

B.

Claims Pertaining to Alteration and Repair of
the Common Property

[
39
]

These claims are particularized in paras. 44-49
of the notice of civil claim and allege the council “turned part of the podium
gardens into an area for planting of vegetables without knowledge and approval
of owners”, the Property Manager failed to disclose the costs and a council
member apparently posted disbursement claims under the “Landscaping” category. Paras.
3 and 4 of the Relief Sought claim the Council Members acted improperly in
proceeding with the work without approval of the owners.

[
40
]

These claims have no merit whatsoever. There is
no claim that the Council Members were in violation of s. 32 of the Act and so
the plaintiff has no statutory ability to advance the claims against the
Council Members and the actions of the council in converting the gardens was
within the authority of the council and did not require owner approval.
Accordingly, paras. 3 and 4 of the Relief Sought are struck and dismissed.

C.

Failure to Repair Common Property Water Problem
in Unit A707

[
41
]

The facts alleged in paras. 50-57 relate to
water ingress in suite A707 which is not owned by the plaintiff but is
allegedly owned by a “relative”. The plaintiff clearly has no standing to sue
for damage to a suite in which he does not have an interest and so this claim,
which is contained in para. 5 of the Relief Sought, is struck and dismissed.

D.

Unapproved and Illegal Installation of Security
Cameras

[
42
]

Paragraphs 58-62 are not clear but it appears as
though there was a resolution of the owners in 2008 to install a security
camera system and the system was never installed, as apparently the cost of the
system may have exceeded the amount council was authorized to spend for the
system. The Relief Sought in paras. 6 and 7 are against the Property Manager
and Council Members for failing to install the system and alleged
misrepresentations. The plaintiff has no standing to pursue a claim against the
Property Manager which had contracted with the strata corporation and the
claims against the Council Members are not within the purview of s. 32 and s.
33 of the Act and accordingly claims 6 and 7 are struck and dismissed.

E.

Improper Installation of Surveillance Cameras in
2009

[
43
]

The allegation here is again somewhat confusing
as there was a further resolution of the owners in 2009 to install surveillance
cameras but that the cameras that were installed were allegedly contrary to the
resolution of 2009. These allegations, which are made in paras. 63-72, seek
declarations that the Property Manager and Council Members breached obligations
owed to the strata corporation. As the plaintiff has no standing to sue the
Property Manager for reasons set out above and as the claims against the Council
Members do not relate to the latter’s obligations under
s. 32
of the
Act
, these
claims, set out in paras. 8-9 of the Relief Sought, are struck and dismissed. As
well, the plaintiff claims in para. 9 of the Relief Sought that installation
and operation of the surveillance camera system was contrary to the provisions
of the
Personal Information Protection Act
however that Act does not
authorize this court to make orders which are within the authority of the
Privacy Commissioner.

F.

Alleged Refusal to give the plaintiff access to
Strata Corporation Records

[
44
]

Paragraphs 73-87 include allegations that the
Council Members and the Property Manager have failed to provide the plaintiff
with access to records of the strata corporation or to maintain them in the
“usual location”, whatever that may mean. The claims are asserted in paras. 10
- 13 of the Relief sought. In this allegation as is the case in several other
allegations, the plaintiff claims a breach by the Property Manager of the
management agreement with the strata corporation in failing to provide the
plaintiff access to certain records. Only the strata corporation can enforce
the property management agreement and accordingly that portion of the
plaintiff’s claim against the Property Manager is dismissed. Likewise, the
claim that the Property Manager store records for viewing in a certain filing
cabinet according to “long-established practice” is without merit and as well
is frivolous and vexatious. The plaintiff has no standing to enforce the
management agreement entered into by the strata corporation on his behalf and
on behalf of all other owners. Finally, once again the claims in these paras.
against the Council Members do not allege a breach of
s. 32
. Accordingly, all
claims in paras. 10-13 are struck and dismissed.

G.

Claims made against the Property Manager for
Reimbursement of Payments made by the Strata Corporation

[
45
]

The claim is asserted in para. 14 of the Relief
Sought and the allegations are included in paras. 88-95 and consist of alleged
payments to the Property Manager for “improperly claimed fees”. This claim is
struck and dismissed as the plaintiff has no standing to bring such an action
which only the strata corporation could commence and maintain.

H.

Claims for Reimbursement of Disbursement Claims
made from the Strata Corporation by Council Members Eddie Chu, Winne Wong and
Vasco Chu

[
46
]

In paras. 96 - 106 of the notice of civil claim
and claims made in paras. 15 - 19 of the Relief Sought the plaintiff seeks
reimbursement to the strata corporation by the directors listed above of
disbursement payments made by the strata corporation to those directors. Some
of the transactions that have been called into question by the plaintiff
involve payments or reimbursements made by the Property Manager to Eddie Chu
which payments were approved by Eddie Chu (NOCC paras. 98-99). Those payments
could be considered as transactions which could be questioned under
sections 32

and
33
of the
Act
as conflicts of interest. It is also not clear whether or not
the strata corporation ratified those transactions under s. 33(1) which would
have approved the payments.

[
47
]

The two payments in question amount to a total
of $727.80. It is possible that in the circumstances this court could find the
payments to be “unreasonable or unfair” to the strata corporation. Accordingly,
I decline to dismiss the claims relating to the payments to Eddie Chu in paras.
98 and 99 of the notice of civil claim.

[
48
]

All other allegations made in paras. 96 to 106
and paras. 15-19 of the Relief Sought do not amount to conflicts of interest
which could be pursued under sections 32 and 33 of the Act and are struck and
dismissed.

I.

Disbursement Claims by the Property Manager

[
49
]

Paras. 107-110 refer to payments to the Property
Manager by the strata corporation to reimburse the Property Manager for
specific expenses. The plaintiff has no standing to be able to claim
reimbursement by the Property Manager as the only person or corporation who has
standing to be able to make that claim is the strata corporation. Accordingly
these claims, which are sough in paras. 18 and 20 of the Relief Sought are struck
and dismissed.

J.

Claim that Eddie Chu has made Unauthorized Use
of Strata Chairs

[
50
]

This claim, which is described in paras. 111 and
112, does not amount to a claim for a breach of sections 32 and 33 which would
allow a claim against a council member. There was no damage alleged to the
strata property and accordingly this claim, which is reflected in para. 25 of
the Relief Sought is struck and dismissed.

K.

Allegations of contravention of Parking Rules by
Eddie Chu, Jimmy Chen and Winne Wong

[
51
]

These allegations are contained in paras.
113-123 of the notice of civil claim and paras. 22-24 of the Relief Sought. The
plaintiff is seeking an order that this court impose a fine on the persons for
parking violations. It is the duty of the strata corporation to enforce the
parking and other rules and regulations and only the strata corporation can
enforce the same, not this court or any individual. Accordingly these claims
are dismissed in full.

L.

Plaintiff’s request for a Council Hearing

[
52
]

These allegations, contained in paras. 124-133
of the notice of civil claim, relate to the council denying the plaintiff’s
requests for a hearing, for interrupting the plaintiff’s discussions at a
council meeting and the plaintiff seeks, in paras. 26 and 27 of the Relief
Sought that the Council Members have breached their obligations under the Act
and that a fine be imposed on a Council Member. I have reviewed these
allegations carefully and cannot decipher a cause of action arising from the
events described. Clearly, the council is able to conduct the business of the
council as it sees fit in accordance with the Act and the rules and if the
plaintiff were to be able to go to court every time he is interrupted in a
meeting, it would amount to a gross waste of time of this court and all
involved. The facts alleged to not amount to a valid cause of action and is
hereby struck and dismissed.

M.

Defamation in March 16, 2011 Council Meeting
Minutes

[
53
]

It is not at all clear from the facts pleaded in
paras. 134 to 145 that the plaintiff is asserting a cause of action. He does
allege the minutes of the meeting are not accurate but his demands have been
denied by the Property Manager and the council. Paragraph 29 of the Relief
Sought seems to amount to a claim for defamation, however, the same could also
be interpreted as a request to change the minutes to reflect what the plaintiff
alleges was actually stated at the meeting. As the allegations now stand, if
there is a claim for defamation against council members, the pleadings are
inadequate but are subject to being clarified through amendment. If the
plaintiff’s claim is for rectification of the minutes, preparation of the
minutes is a duty within the purview of the council and does not give rise to a
cause of action and accordingly that portion of the claim would be struck and
dismissed.

N.

Council Meeting of May 4, 2011 and Undisclosed
Audio Recording

[
54
]

The complaint in paras. 146-175 relate to the
use by the council of a recording device at the meeting and not obtaining the
consent of those present at the meeting for use of the device. The plaintiff
has made a complaint to the Privacy Commissioner however no order has been made
by that office. There is no known cause of action claimed in the paragraphs
referred to above. I agree with counsel for the defendants that the claim is
unnecessary and vexatious and it is hereby struck and dismissed. The dismissal
also includes any claim for defamation arising from the “Report on
Harrassement” referred to in paras. 169 to 172 and para. 32 of the Relief
Sought.

O.

Assault by Eddie Chu and refusal of Access to an
Office

[
55
]

As is the case with most of the notice of civil
claim, it is very difficult to understand what the plaintiff seeks in this
section, ie. paras. 176 to 181 save for his allegation of assault against Eddie
Chu. If so, there is no allegation of any injury to the plaintiff. For this
portion of the claim to proceed, there would have to be an amendment to the
claim. (
Friedmann v. Thompson
2010 BCCA 277
).

P.

Settlement by council regarding Insurance
Deductible

[
56
]

It is alleged in paras. 182-186 that the strata
corporation paid a deductible amount on an insurance claim and then compromised
on a claim for reimbursement against the owner of the unit in issue. These
allegations do not give rise to a cause of action. The strata corporation was
entitled to compromise a claim and there was no personal loss to the plaintiff
as a result. This claim is struck and dismissed as well.

Q.

Alleged Improprieties at May 27, 2011 AGM

[
57
]

Paragraphs 187 to 204 allege various voting
improprieties at the meeting of May 27, 2011 including rejection of some proxy
forms, tactics to interfere with the plaintiff’s questions and failure to
prepare accurate minutes. Paragraph 39 of the Relief Sought is a claim for a
declaration that the Council Members breached the bylaws and that this court
impose fines as a result. It is not up to the court to impose fines against the
defendants, that is within the purview of only the council and strata corporation.

[
58
]

Regarding the alleged voting irregularities
during the 2011 AGM, the defendants submit that if there were any
irregularities, the same have been remedied by the subsequent 2012 AGM at which
the owners elected a new council and also approved a new budget. As is the case
with most of the claim of the plaintiff, it is not at all clear what he is
seeking or there is little if any relationship between the facts alleged and
any relief which is sought. I cannot decipher from the pleadings any cause of
action known at law and accordingly the claims described in paras. 187-204 are
struck and dismissed.

R.

Alleged Interference with the Plaintiff and
Assault of June 20, 2011

[
59
]

The complaint relates to alleged interference by
the Council Members in an attempt by the plaintiff to inspect a video recorder
and a power washer in June of 2011 and can be found at paras. 205 to 211 of the
notice of civil claim.  The plaintiff seeks in para. 40 of the Claims Sought a
declaration that certain Council Members interfered with his efforts and also
seeks an order that a fine imposed on the plaintiff is invalid. To the extent
these allegations amount to a claim against the Council Members, there is no
allegation of conflict of interest or any of the other requirements for an action
against Council Members as prescribed in sections 32 and 33. Regarding the
strata corporation, if the plaintiff is alleging the strata corporation is not
enforcing its bylaws and should have fined the Council Members involved, that
is not specifically claimed and even if it could, the imposition of fines is
within the jurisdiction of the strata corporation and not the courts. These
claims accordingly have no possibility of success and are struck and dismissed.

S.

Complaints regarding August 24, 2011 Council
Meeting

[
60
]

In paras. 216-224 of the notice of civil claim,
the plaintiff claims interference with his presentation to the meeting of
August 24, 2011 and that council members used foul language when dealing with
the plaintiff. Again, in paras. 41 and 42 of the Relief Sought, the plaintiff
seeks, among other relief, a declaration of the Council Members having breached
the bylaws, an imposition of fines on the Council members and a declaration
that a fine imposed on the plaintiff is invalid. As stated by counsel for the
defendants, it is likely open for the plaintiff to attempt to amend his claim
to allege that the fine imposed against him by the strata corporation was
“significantly unfair” to the plaintiff contrary to
s. 64
of the
Act
. However,
it is highly unlikely that the court would interfere with the power of the
strata corporation to impose a fine. To the extent the claim is against the
Council Members that claim is hereby struck and dismissed as not contemplated
by
sections 32
or
33
of the Act.

T.

Defamation in August 27, 2011 Council meeting
Minutes

[
61
]

Paras. 225 to 227 allege the plaintiff was
defamed by the words of the minutes of the August 27, 2011 council meeting by
stating “the abusive and insulting actions directed at staff, and the rude and
hostile conduct towards other owners.” In para. 43 of the Relief Sought the
plaintiff seeks a declaration against the Council Members that they had
publicized the defamatory words and seeks damages. This is not a claim under
the
Act
. If the plaintiff wishes to continue with the claim for defamation, the
pleadings will have to be expanded and amended to comply with the Rules of
Court.

U.

Change in Colour of the Exterior Walls

[
62
]

The strata corporation obtained a resolution in
May of 2011 to re-paint the exterior of the building. It is presumed that the
plaintiff did not approve of the change in colour of the exterior of the
building as he is alleging that the strata corporation through the Council
Members was not authorized to change the colour. He seeks a declaration and an
order that the Council Members pay damages to the strata corporation as a
result of the unauthorized change in colour. To the extent this is a claim
against the Council Members, it is not authorized by
sections 32
and
33
and the
plaintiff has no standing to bring an action seeking the payment of damages to
the strata corporation. Also, the strata corporation was authorized to paint
the building as it wished and every detail of work need not be approved by the
owners. These claims are struck and dismissed.

V.

CLAIMS IN ACTION NO. 145263

[
63
]

This is a second action commenced against the
Property Manager and its representatives as well as individual council members.
The strata corporation is not a defendant in this second action.

[
64
]

As stated by counsel for the defendants, there
are claims in this action which come under two general classes of complaint.

[
65
]

The first class of complaint is in respect of
allegations of access for the plaintiff to the records of the strata
corporation. Regarding this claim, which is set out in paras. 13-34, counsel
for the defendant has summarized the claims as follows:

a)         declarations
that the defendants acted improperly in respect of strata documents;

b)         an
order requiring the defendants to “restore a grandfather practice” and maintain
records in a particular loaction within the strata building; and

c)         an order that
the strata council members and the Property Manager repay finds associated with
hiring a lawyer to address document issues to the strata corporation.

[
66
]

The plaintiff has no standing to make a claim
against the Property Manager regarding duties allegedly owed by the Property
Manager to the strata corporation and there is no alleged conflict per
section
32
of the
Act
which could justify an action against the Council Members.

[
67
]

All claims in respect of the strata corporation
records are without merit and the plaintiff has no standing to bring that claim
which are frivolous and vexatious claims and are struck and dismissed.

[
68
]

The second general class of complaint relates to
an alleged deactivation of keyfobs that had been issued to the plaintiff and to
owners of other strata lots. Deactivation of the keyfobs was a decision of the
strata corporation and the strata corporation is not a defendant in this
action. Even if the claims in the second action were to be amended and the
strata corporation were added as a defendant, there is no allegation that he
plaintiff in particular has received “significantly unfair” treatment by the
strata corporation and so such an amendment would fail.

[
69
]

Accordingly all of the allegations relating to
the keyfob deactivation are struck and dismissed as are all other allegations
in action no. 145263.

[
70
]

Finally, the defendants are entitled to their
costs of the action to date. I will receive submissions as to the appropriate
scale of costs, such submissions to be received by October 15, 2013.

“Jenkins
J.”
